// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=NewtonsoftJson&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;

// Everything here runs once, when the test assembly loads, before any test.
public static class ModuleInitializer
{
    [ModuleInitializer]
    public static void Initialize()
    {
        // Initializes every Verify.* plugin the project references and has not initialized above.
        // Explicit calls come first so their parameters apply: a plugin can only be initialized once.
        VerifierSettings.InitializePlugins();
    }
}

==== src/VerifySample.Tests/Plugins/NewtonsoftJsonTests.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=NewtonsoftJson&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using Newtonsoft.Json.Linq;

// Verify.NewtonsoftJson: Writes Newtonsoft.Json JObject and JArray values as readable json, instead of as their object graphs.
// https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.NewtonsoftJson
// Note: This is the Newtonsoft counterpart to Verify.SystemJson: both solve the "json DOM type"
// problem, for different json stacks.
// Note: VerifyNewtonsoftJson exposes only Initialize(). There are no settings methods, scrubbers
// or per test options.
// Note: Json parsed into these types is still scrubbed by Verify's own counters, so a Guid or a
// date inside it is replaced.
public class NewtonsoftJsonTests
{
    // Verify serializes with Argon, a Newtonsoft.Json fork, so a JObject is otherwise written
    // as its internal node graph. This converter writes the json it represents.
    [Fact]
    public Task JsonObject()
    {
        var target = JObject.Parse(
            """
            {
              "Property1": "Value1",
              "Property2": 42
            }
            """);
        return Verify(target);
    }

    // A JArray is handled by its own converter, and lands in the snapshot as a list.
    [Fact]
    public Task JsonArray()
    {
        var target = JArray.Parse(
            """
            ["Small", "Medium", "Large"]
            """);
        return Verify(target);
    }

    // JToken.Parse returns whichever node type the json holds, so the same call covers an
    // object, an array or a scalar.
    [Fact]
    public Task JsonToken()
    {
        var target = JToken.Parse(
            """
            {
              "Nested": {
                "Property": "Value"
              }
            }
            """);
        return Verify(target);
    }
}
